Think of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model like a specialized traffic control center. Instead of one giant brain handling every single car, you have many smaller, specialized experts. When a car approaches, only the relevant experts wake up to make a decision, while the rest stay asleep. This saves massive amounts of energy and processing power.

For a laptop chip, this is crucial. Traditional models try to process everything at once, requiring huge, power-hungry hardware. MoE allows the model to be incredibly large in total knowledge but very small in active computation for any given task. It’s like having a library of millions of books, but only checking out the one you need.
